investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' for both nodes that carry the resource, and preemption found no victims, indicating all slots are occupied by existing pods with no lower-priority candidates to evict.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or point to a node label that has changed, the effective capacity is further constrained.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have been scaled out to meet concurrent eval or production demand, causing all slots to be consumed before the eval pod could be admitted.

Lower confidence — transient slot leak or stuck pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations without releasing them: if previously scheduled remote-agent pods are in a terminal but non-releasing state, their resource reservations would block new scheduling even if the workload is complete.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-08T07:11–07:16Z), 0 of 6 nodes were schedulable for new remote agent pods: the 2 nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never completed, the probe timed out after ~131–152 seconds, and zero required evidence fields were written, causing all three checks to fail with identical scheduler rejection messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods nodes satisfy, so even if vm slots were freed on the other 4 nodes, those pods could not be scheduled there.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning or scale-out lag: the cluster may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, and auto-scaling (if configured) did not add capacity within the eval timeout window.

Lower confidence — eval probe scheduling contention: all three sibling checks ran nearly simultaneously (07:11–07:16Z), potentially competing for the same limited vm slots and collectively exhausting capacity faster than any single run would.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

If the eval runner logs show an API-level error (e.g., 4xx/5xx from the agent creation endpoint) before the scheduler message, the root cause would be upstream of the Kubernetes scheduler.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No pod was ever started, so the eval runner received no response and produced zero evidence, causing a total contract gap for all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~131–152 s across all three checks). Because no pod ever reaches a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returns an agent, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (check-expectations.json lines 266–270) receives an empty evidence object, failing all five required evidence assertions. This is an eval-layer signal of a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the extended VM resource type used by peer-pod (kata containers) is fully consumed, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. All three sibling checks report the identical scheduler message, confirming this is not an isolated pod issue.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the affinity were relaxed or more matching nodes were available, scheduling might succeed.

TERTIARY — Cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, it may not have triggered or completed before the eval timeout (~142 s), causing the pod to remain unscheduled.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Leaked or unreleased kata VM slots from a prior eval run: if a previous probe run did not clean up remote agent pods (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), residual pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, artificially exhausting capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks report the identical Unschedulable scheduler event citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 affinity-matching nodes. This is the earliest violated boundary in the eval execution path.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and making the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion immediately impactful.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity vs. consumed slots on the 2 affinity-matching nodes. This is the highest-priority action to confirm or resolve the outage.
Check for leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up. If found, terminate them and re-run the eval to verify recovery.

If kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is genuinely exhausted by production workloads (not eval leaks), assess whether additional kata-capable nodes can be added to the cluster or whether the node affinity can be relaxed to include more of the 6 available nodes.
Review whether cluster autoscaling is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm node pools and, if so, why it did not provision additional capacity before the eval timeout (~142 s).

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in features.json (lines 183–184) and both failed, confirm the feature's degraded/outage status against the degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds (lines 187–188) and escalate if appropriate.
Note: remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false (features.json line 185), so its failure alone does not trigger a feature outage declaration, but the two required sibling failures do.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and not exhausted on the affinity-matching nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime probe immediately after this failure, with no cluster changes, would suggest the failure was transient rather than a persistent capacity shortage.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity was misconfigured (e.g., selecting zero nodes) and that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was not actually exhausted would shift the root cause to a configuration error rather than resource exhaustion.

Scheduler logs showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota, network policy) would narrow or redirect the diagnosis.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state on a different cluster or environment would confirm the issue is cluster-specific rather than a code or API regression.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct, actionable signal rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 1 node with available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots), catching affinity misconfigurations early.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote agent pods from prior eval runs are left in Running or Pending state after withCleanup completes, detecting resource leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a latency-banded eval that distinguishes between a pod that never scheduled (Unschedulable) and one that scheduled but timed out during VM readiness, enabling more precise triage of future remote-agent failures.
